title: Bodhisattva at the Gas Station: Studying the Ways of the Bodhisattva
speaker: Nomon Tim Burnett
summary: Nomon Tim Burnett introduces the bodhisattva path as the theme for the rest of the year and lays out the traditional six practices: generosity, ethical living, patience, energy, meditative concentration, and wisdom, recommending Dale Wright's book The Six Perfections. Nomon tells a story on Nomon's own part: after teaching multitasking in Seattle, Nomon leaves late for a 2:30 meeting, starts the pump, buys a coupon latte, and drives off with the gas hose still attached. The station manager pats Nomon's shoulder, says "Perhaps you are a little stressed," and trusts Nomon with just a name on a pad. Nomon connects the manager to the Chinese ancestor Joshu, who vowed to learn from a seven-year-old girl, then asks the room where they have met bodhisattvas lately, drawing answers about a band called Out of the Ashes and a Brian Doyle reading.

Probably emerged right around the birth of Christ around that time, but nobody really knows.
It's the ideal of being a person whose goal is to serve all beings.

The thing about that, right away though, we have to be a little careful because in our cultural and historical moment when we think about serving other people, we end up sometimes harming yourself, and that's not what they meant.
There's a famous story which I've heard from enough sources, probably is true, and that there was a Dalai Lama likes to talk to scientists, and he's really interested in science somehow.

He had this little car—I don't know how it got into Lhasa—we had this little car which he actually took apart and put back together as a young little roadster with an open top.

That's neither here nor there, but one of the early meetings with psychology and looking for what are the connections and overlaps and agreements and also what are the disagreements between this Tibetan Buddhist system of understanding the mind in reality.
How does that connect or not connect to science?
One of things I love about his intention is that he's also interested in what the way is that it doesn't, they don't match.

That's pretty great anyway.

One time, one of these early meetings with some cognitive scientists and psychologists and Western meditation teachers, they were talking about compassion, which is one of the main things that bodhisattvas practice.
